classification.difficultyReason: Select identities to obtain trigonometric quadratics, handle half-angle and double-angle domains, reject invalid roots, and round non-exact angles to minutes; hints supply the reframing in g–h.

content.prompt: Solve, for $0^\circ\leq\theta\leq360^\circ$, giving solutions correct to the nearest minute where necessary:

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}3(1-2\sin^2\theta)+\sin\theta&=1\\6\sin^2\theta-\sin\theta-2&=0\\(3\sin\theta-2)(2\sin\theta+1)&=0\\\sin\theta&=\frac23\quad\text{or}\quad-\frac12\end{aligned}$$
For $\sin\theta=\frac23$, $\theta\approx41^\circ49',138^\circ11'$.

For $\sin\theta=-\frac12$, $\theta=210^\circ,330^\circ$.

Thus $\theta=41^\circ49',138^\circ11',210^\circ,330^\circ$, to the nearest minute where necessary.

$$\begin{aligned}\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta&=3\cos^2\theta-2\sin^2\theta\\2\cos^2\theta&=\sin^2\theta\end{aligned}$$
When $\cos\theta=0$, this gives $0=1$, so $90^\circ$ and $270^\circ$ are not solutions. Divide by $\cos^2\theta$:
$$\begin{aligned}\tan^2\theta&=2\\\tan\theta&=\pm\sqrt2\end{aligned}$$
Hence $\theta\approx54^\circ44',125^\circ16',234^\circ44',305^\circ16'$.

$$\begin{aligned}10\left(2\cos^2\frac\theta2-1\right)+13\cos\frac\theta2&=5\\20\cos^2\frac\theta2+13\cos\frac\theta2-15&=0\\\left(4\cos\frac\theta2+5\right)\left(5\cos\frac\theta2-3\right)&=0\\\cos\frac\theta2&=\frac35\quad\text{or}\quad-\frac54\end{aligned}$$
Reject $-\frac54$, which is outside the range of cosine. Since $0^\circ\leq\frac\theta2\leq180^\circ$,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac\theta2&=\cos^{-1}\frac35\\\theta&=2\cos^{-1}\frac35\\\theta&\approx106^\circ16'.\end{aligned}$$

The original equation excludes $\theta=90^\circ,180^\circ,270^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{2\tan\frac\theta2}{1-\tan^2\frac\theta2}&=3\tan\frac\theta2\\2\tan\frac\theta2&=3\tan\frac\theta2\left(1-\tan^2\frac\theta2\right)\\\tan\frac\theta2\left(2-3+3\tan^2\frac\theta2\right)&=0\\\tan\frac\theta2\left(3\tan^2\frac\theta2-1\right)&=0\\\tan\frac\theta2&=0\quad\text{or}\quad\pm\frac1{\sqrt3}\end{aligned}$$
For $0^\circ\leq\frac\theta2\leq180^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\frac\theta2=0:&\quad\frac\theta2=0^\circ,180^\circ,\quad\theta=0^\circ,360^\circ\\\tan\frac\theta2=\frac1{\sqrt3}:&\quad\frac\theta2=30^\circ,\quad\theta=60^\circ\\\tan\frac\theta2=-\frac1{\sqrt3}:&\quad\frac\theta2=150^\circ,\quad\theta=300^\circ\end{aligned}$$
All four satisfy the original equation. Thus $\theta=0^\circ,60^\circ,300^\circ,360^\circ$.

$$\begin{aligned}\cos2\theta+3\cos^2\theta+3\sin^2\theta&=3\sin2\theta\\\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta+3\cos^2\theta+3\sin^2\theta&=3\sin2\theta\\4\cos^2\theta+2\sin^2\theta&=6\sin\theta\cos\theta\\4\cos^2\theta-6\sin\theta\cos\theta+2\sin^2\theta&=0\\2(2\cos\theta-\sin\theta)(\cos\theta-\sin\theta)&=0\end{aligned}$$
When $\cos\theta=0$, the fourth line has left side $2$, so $90^\circ$ and $270^\circ$ are not solutions. Dividing the factors by $\cos\theta$ gives
$$\tan\theta=2\quad\text{or}\quad\tan\theta=1.$$
For $\tan\theta=2$, $\theta\approx63^\circ26',243^\circ26'$.

For $\tan\theta=1$, $\theta=45^\circ,225^\circ$.

Thus $\theta=45^\circ,63^\circ26',225^\circ,243^\circ26'$, to the nearest minute where necessary.
